      "observations": [
        "Read all 5,838 lines of the exact eligible owned diff across all 18 paths. This replaces callback-returned abortable objects with Promise-returning functions and AbortSignal inputs across the historical wizard, Account Hub view, ordinary config sources, Exchange discovery, HTTP helper and socket guessing. It removes the old Abortable/ParallelCall/PriorityOrder/OAuth wrapper exports. The later modernization, generic Error replacement and broader tests remain separate assigned entries.",
        "The new promiseFirstSuccessful awaits already-started promises in input order, aborts the supplied controller after an ordered winner and consumes remaining rejections; all-failed work ends in Promise.any's aggregate rejection. Its documentation describes the controller as optional, but the implementation calls abortController.abort unconditionally on success; inspected production callers supply it. Existing ordered-priority knowledge is reused, not re-created as a fastest-response rule.",
        "FindConfig starts disk/ISP/database/MX with a combined internal/external signal and gives Exchange the external signal. Exchange enrichment therefore outlives ordinary-source cancellation. This existing focused lesson is reused. The owned generator handles redirect confirmation through promise resolvers and has its own error/result policy; the accepted generator later uses allSettled plus an explicit aborted-result null check. Those phases are not treated as identical.",
        "Disk reading changes to IOUtils.exists/readUTF8 with cancellation checks around I/O. Provider and MX helpers start ordered fetch candidates with combined signals, and DNS completion checks the signal before consuming records. Provider XML-to-AccountConfig parsing happens after selecting a fetched response; this is not a claim that every prior callback failure/fallback behavior is unchanged.",
        "fetchHTTP becomes an async XMLHttpRequest wrapper with URLSearchParams, serialized upload bodies, UTF-8 Basic-auth byte conversion, timeout/user signal composition, redirect retry and structured HTTP/parse/network errors. The owned cache/auth-prompt/secure-auth branches also change, so this is not pure syntax modernization. The accepted helper later drops those old cache/prompt/secure-auth options and guards optional/pre-aborted signals before request creation. Numeric HTTP status versus -2 network fallback and -4 parse failure are scoped existing knowledge, not fresh execution.",
        "The owned HTTP helper puts args.signal directly in AbortSignal.any despite documenting it optional. The accepted helper builds a list only from a present signal and calls throwIfAborted before creating the request. The later accepted test directly checks exact pre-abort reason and no recorded request, and separately checks wrapped in-flight abort metadata. Those later tests are not credited to this landing or executed here.",
        "Exchange OAuth acquisition registers prompt cancellation on the signal. A cancelled acquisition throws UserCancelledException rather than selecting Basic auth; ordinary token acquisition failure can use Basic auth. The returned HTTP promise is not awaited inside that token-acquisition try block, so that catch is not a general fallback for every later HTTP failure. Untrusted cross-domain redirects await a cancellable delay, confirmation promise and post-confirmation signal check.",
        "An exact remaining XML RedirectAddr call-contract mismatch is visible in both the owned change and fixed accepted source: fetchConfigFromExchange takes abortSignal third, while its recursive readAutoDiscoverResponse call supplies username || emailAddress third and abortSignal last. The third parameter is consumed by AbortSignal.any. The main FindConfig caller uses the new order correctly. The inspected redirect test is HTTP 301, not an XML RedirectAddr scenario; no XML redirect was run.",
        "AddonInstaller now takes an AbortSignal, installs/removes a bound cancellation listener around direct installation and retains add-on enabling/startup waiting afterward. Account Hub passes controller.signal. The historical accountSetup caller instead passes the AbortController itself. A matching already-active add-on can return before direct-install listener use, so the concern is bounded to the path needing installation. The legacy file is absent at the fixed accepted revision; no install failure or Owl authentication was reproduced.",
        "HostDetector/HostTry become classes with combined cancellation, ordered result selection and index-based staggered starts. Host selection is not promiseFirstSuccessful because incoming discovery may need an alternative protocol too. _processResult returns an explicit retry Boolean and #runTry retries once, rechecks cancellation and rejects non-success. Socket abort closes the transport; the input pump's stop/data/error callbacks settle the returned promise. Engine socket, proxy, timer and TLS implementations remain unread.",
        "Read every owned changed test hunk. The new utility file has nine direct assertion sites covering chosen result/index, controller abortion, ordered aggregate errors, timeout lower bounds/error message and exact explicit-abort reason; all have nonempty expected-behavior messages containing Should/should. It does not force a lower-priority success to beat a pending higher-priority promise or cover every already-aborted timer/listener-cleanup case. The accepted leftover-rejection test is later code.",
        "FetchConfig/FindConfig/GuessConfig tests adopt signals and new async/result shapes. The provider-via-MX task replaces canned FetchHTTP instances with local HTTP servers behind HTTPS proxies, mocks DNS, checks config/source fields and sorts actual request URLs because arrival order is unstable. Its direct config/request assertions and DNS mock assertion omit messages. Existing socket/config field assertions in touched tests also retain message gaps; no new assertions were authored here.",
        "The redirect-rejection assertion expects null after next({ acceptRedirect: false }) but says invalid email address in its message. This is a concrete expected-condition mismatch, not merely missing should. The test directly checks redirect host/scheme and returned config; it does not validate the XML-address recursion branch.",
        "The public certificate specification adds autoconfig.test.test to the SAN list. Static certificate metadata parsing confirms that added name while subject, issuer and validity dates remain as declared. Old/new certificate, spec and binary-key blobs/byte sizes are recorded; post-change blobs equal the fixed accepted blobs. Certificate text diff and binary-change metadata were inspected, while key internals and cryptographic coherence/chain/signature validity were not tested. No certificate/key payload is quoted in a lesson.",
        "The Account Hub test fixes its Cancel-label message and directly checks label/control state after clicking Cancel; this is not a network-cancellation or add-on-installation oracle. The Exchange browser fixture uses the actual comm MailStringUtils UTF-8/ByteString conversion when building expected Basic-auth bytes. No browser UI, accessibility tree, real credential flow or TLS connection was exercised.",
        "Read full D277843 timeline and all five actual inline bodies, including the nullable-to-Boolean _processResult suggestion and hanlde-to-handle comment correction. Actual source adopts both exact corrections. Preserve the author's possible Windows/manual-config failure report, later Try report without those failures, renewed review for email.mjs, reset/abort concern and author's changed-flow response, acceptance/rebases and early-cycle landing choice as historical discussion. Done/approval is not fresh validation of the reset or fallback behavior.",
        "Reuse the complete parent Bug 2008517 context already read with 4378. It separates the three refactors, explicitly gives weaker Owl-installation coverage, later reports QA of both UIs on named platforms and prompt flow, and supplies no Owl-authentication result. Related later regressions, CI links, licensing/account-access discussion and external protocol specifications remain bounded context; no dependency chase or official writes.",

The author separates the three refactors and explicitly gives weaker Owl-installation coverage. Later QA reports both UIs/platforms and the prompt flow, with no Owl-authentication result.",

Owned code adopts these corrections. Reset-related concerns and the author's changed-flow response remain discussion, not a verified reset guarantee.",
        "The author's first stack Try report suspects Windows manual-config failure; a later report says another Try no longer showed those failures and re-requests review for email.mjs. Review acceptance, rebases, historical remote completion reports and early-cycle landing are preserved separately. No linked job or additional review dependency was read.",
        "All owned functional/test hunks and necessary fixed accepted callers are inspected. The XML recursion argument mismatch, historical wizard controller/signal mismatch and incorrect redirect-rejection message are exact static findings. Separate existing lessons cover ordered priority, Exchange enrichment lifetime, Hub cancellation/fallback and numeric HTTP status. No runtime, TLS, authentication, installer or test result is inferred.",

Linked later regressions and protocols remain bounded unread dependencies."
